## Fire risk assessments across Scotland

We are based at 272 Bath Street in Glasgow and carry out fire risk assessments in every part of Scotland, from city-centre tenements to island guest houses. Travel is included in your fixed quote. 

In short: Fire Risk Scotland covers all 32 Scottish council areas from our Glasgow office, including Glasgow, Edinburgh, Aberdeen, Dundee, Inverness, Stirling, Perth, the Highlands and the islands. Every assessment is carried out in person by Raj Chall BSc, and fixed fees from £225 + VAT include travel.

Mainland Scotland, Orkney and the Western Isles, plotted by latitude and longitude. Lines show travel from our Glasgow office. We also cover Shetland.

### Glasgow and the west

Our office is in Glasgow city centre, so Glasgow, East and West Dunbartonshire, Renfrewshire, East Renfrewshire, Inverclyde and North and South Lanarkshire are covered with the shortest notice. Much of the work here is HMOs in tenement flats, city-centre offices and shops, and common closes for factors.

### Ayrshire, Lanarkshire and Renfrewshire

North, South and East Ayrshire, including Ayr, Kilmarnock, Irvine and the coast, plus Paisley, Greenock, Hamilton, Motherwell, East Kilbride and Lanark. Coastal guest houses and holiday lets are common here, alongside industrial units and town-centre shops.

### Fife and the Lothians

Fife, including Dunfermline, Kirkcaldy, Glenrothes and St Andrews, and West Lothian, Midlothian and East Lothian, including Livingston, Dalkeith, Musselburgh and North Berwick. St Andrews has a large stock of student HMOs and holiday lets.

Stirling, Falkirk, Clackmannanshire and the surrounding towns. Work here includes tourist accommodation around the Trossachs and Loch Lomond, offices, schools and community buildings.

Dundee, Perth and Kinross, and Angus, including Arbroath, Montrose, Forfar, Crieff and Pitlochry. Dundee's student population means a high number of HMOs, while Perthshire has many hotels, guest houses and holiday lets.

### Aberdeen and the north-east

Aberdeen City, Aberdeenshire and Moray, including Peterhead, Fraserburgh, Inverurie, Stonehaven, Huntly and Elgin. Work includes offices, industrial premises, HMOs and rural tourist accommodation.

### Inverness, Highlands and islands

Inverness and the Highland Council area, Argyll and Bute, the Western Isles, Orkney and Shetland. Guest houses, hotels, bunkhouses, self-catering lets and community halls make up much of the work. We plan Highland and island visits efficiently and can group several properties into one trip.

### The Borders and Dumfries and Galloway

The Scottish Borders, including Galashiels, Hawick, Kelso and Peebles, and Dumfries and Galloway, including Dumfries, Stranraer, Castle Douglas and Kirkcudbright. Rural holiday lets, guest houses, farm buildings and town-centre premises are typical.

Do you cover the north of England?
Fire Risk Scotland specialises in Scottish premises and Scottish fire law. Our sister company, Scottish Energy Services, works across Scotland and the north of England for energy assessments and building compliance.

## Fire risk assessments in Glasgow

Our office is at 272 Bath Street, in Glasgow city centre. We assess HMOs, tenement closes, short-term lets, offices, shops, bars and restaurants across the city and surrounding council areas.

By Raj Chall BSc, IFE-registered fire risk assessor. Updated 12 November 2026. 

In short: Fire Risk Scotland is based in Glasgow city centre at 272 Bath Street, G2 4JR. We carry out fire risk assessments across Glasgow and the surrounding council areas, with fixed fees from £225 + VAT and your report within 48 hours of the visit. Call 0141 255 1360.

### Fire risk assessments we carry out in Glasgow

- 

#### HMOs

Shared flats and houses needing an HMO licence from Glasgow City Council, including student HMOs.
 
- 

#### Tenement closes

Common closes, stairs and back courts for factors, owners' associations and housing associations.
 
- 

#### Short-term lets

Serviced apartments and holiday lets needing a short-term let licence.
 
- 

#### Offices and shops

City-centre offices, retail units and mixed-use buildings with flats above.
 
- 

#### Bars and restaurants

Licensed premises with commercial kitchens, cellars and late-night occupancy.
 
- 

#### Hotels and guest houses

Hotels, hostels, guest houses and student accommodation.

### Glasgow's buildings and what they mean for fire safety

Much of Glasgow's housing and commercial space is in traditional sandstone tenements: four storeys or more, with a single common close and stair serving every flat. With only one way out, the condition of the stair, the flat entrance doors that open onto it, and anything stored in the close matter more than in almost any other type of building.

Ground-floor shops, bars and takeaways below residential flats are common across the city. In these mixed-use buildings, the business is a relevant premises under the Fire (Scotland) Act 2005 and its fire risk assessment must consider the people living above, especially where the shop's kitchen or storage is next to the residential stair.

Glasgow City Council licenses HMOs and short-term lets in the city, and fire safety is part of both licensing schemes. If you are applying or renewing, tell us so the report covers what the council asks for.

### Why local matters

- 

#### Based in the city

Our Bath Street office means short travel times across Glasgow and the west.
 
- 

#### Report in 48 hours

Useful when a licence deadline or an insurer's request is close.
 
- 

#### One assessor

Raj Chall BSc visits and writes every report himself.

### Areas around Glasgow we cover

Glasgow City, Paisley, Renfrew, Clydebank, Bearsden, Milngavie, Bishopbriggs, Kirkintilloch, Cumbernauld, Coatbridge, Airdrie, Motherwell, Hamilton, East Kilbride, Rutherglen, Newton Mearns, Barrhead, Greenock, Dumbarton and the wider west of Scotland.

### Frequently asked questions

How much is a fire risk assessment in Glasgow?
From £225 + VAT for smaller premises such as an HMO flat, small office or shop. Larger premises, tenement common areas and hotels are quoted individually. The fee is fixed before the visit.

Can you assess an HMO in Glasgow before my licence renewal?
Yes. We recommend booking well ahead of the renewal date so there is time to complete any actions before the application goes in.

Do you assess tenement closes for factors in Glasgow?
Yes. We carry out common area fire risk assessments of tenement closes, stairs, back courts and bin stores for factors, owners and housing associations, following BS 9792:2025.

# Fire Risk Assessment Edinburgh | Short-Term Lets, HMOs, Listed Buildings | Fire Risk Scotland
URL: https://fireriskscotland.com/fire-risk-assessment-edinburgh/

- Home
- Areas we cover
- Edinburgh

## Fire risk assessments in Edinburgh

Short-term lets, HMOs, guest houses, offices and shops across Edinburgh, including the listed buildings of the Old Town and New Town. Assessed in person and written to Scottish fire law.

By Raj Chall BSc, IFE-registered fire risk assessor. Updated 12 November 2026. 

In short: we carry out fire risk assessments across the City of Edinburgh for short-term let hosts, HMO landlords, guest houses, hotels, offices and shops. Fixed fees start from £225 + VAT, and your report is issued within 48 hours of the visit.

### Short-term lets in Edinburgh

Edinburgh has one of the highest concentrations of short-term lets in Scotland, and two sets of rules apply to them. Every short-term let needs a licence from the City of Edinburgh Council, with fire safety as a mandatory condition. Separately, the whole council area has been a short-term let control area since 5 September 2022, so using a property that is not your main home as a short-term let needs planning permission.

Our short-term let assessments give you the fire risk assessment the licence condition requires, with clear actions and the guest fire safety information you need to display.

More about short-term let fire risk assessments

### What we assess in Edinburgh

- 

#### Short-term lets

Whole-property lets, serviced apartments and rooms let in a lived-in home.
 
- 

#### HMOs

Student and professional HMOs needing a licence from the council.
 
- 

#### Guest houses and hotels

Guest houses, B&Bs, hostels and hotels, with their higher sleeping risk.
 
- 

#### Offices and shops

Workplaces, retail units and mixed-use buildings.

### Listed and historic buildings

Many Edinburgh premises are in listed buildings in the Old Town and New Town. The Scottish Government's fire safety guidance recognises that, in a listed building, alternatives to conventional fire safety measures may be appropriate. Original doors, panelling and stairs can often be kept, with the risk managed through upgraded detection, careful fire stopping, or management measures instead. We look for proportionate solutions that protect people without unnecessary damage to the building, and we flag where listed building consent may be needed for any work.

### Festival season

Occupancy in guest houses, short-term lets and venues rises sharply in August. If your premises will be used differently or by more people during the festivals, the fire risk assessment should reflect that, so book a review well before the season starts.

### Frequently asked questions

Do I need a fire risk assessment for an Edinburgh short-term let licence?
Yes. Fire safety is a mandatory condition of every short-term let licence in Scotland, and fire safety law requires the person in charge of the accommodation to carry out a fire risk assessment and keep it under review. Planning permission in the Edinburgh control area is a separate requirement.

How much is a fire risk assessment in Edinburgh?
From £225 + VAT for smaller premises such as a holiday let, HMO flat or small office. Larger premises, hotels and listed buildings with complex layouts are quoted individually, with travel included.

Can you assess a listed building without recommending changes that harm it?
Yes. Scottish Government guidance allows alternatives to conventional measures in listed buildings. We look for proportionate solutions, such as improved detection or management measures, and flag anything that may need listed building consent.

Written and reviewed by Raj Chall BSc, lead fire risk assessor at Fire Risk Scotland, listed on the Institution of Fire Engineers fire risk assessor register. Last reviewed 12 November 2026. This page is general guidance, not legal advice.

## About Fire Risk Scotland

A specialist fire risk assessment company, set up to do one thing well: fire risk assessments for Scottish premises, written to Scottish law, by an assessor you can check. 

### Raj Chall BSc, lead fire risk assessor

Raj has worked in the fire safety industry for 15 years. He holds a BSc and is listed on the Institution of Fire Engineers (IFE) fire risk assessor register, one of the professional registers the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service lists for duty holders choosing an assessor.
 
- BSc
- IFE fire risk assessor register
- 15 years in fire safety

Raj carries out every Fire Risk Scotland assessment in person and writes every report himself. The person who walks your building, opens the plant room and talks to your staff is the person who decides the risk rating and writes the action plan. If you have a question about the report, you speak to him.

### How we work

- 

#### Scottish law, not borrowed English templates

Every report is written to the Fire (Scotland) Act 2005 and the Fire Safety (Scotland) Regulations 2006, using Scottish Government guidance.
 
- 

#### Specific to your premises

No generic reports. The assessment describes your building, your occupants and your risks.
 
- 

#### Proportionate actions

Actions are ranked by priority, explained in plain English, and sized to the actual risk, not to what a contractor might want to sell.
 
- 

#### Fixed fees

From £225 + VAT, agreed before the visit, with travel included.
 
- 

#### Fast reports

Your written report within 48 hours of the site visit, and urgent issues raised on the day.
 
- 

#### Honest about scope

We tell you what an assessment covers and what it does not, and when you need a different specialist.

### Part of Scottish Energy Services

Fire Risk Scotland is a sister company of Scottish Energy Services, the Glasgow energy and building compliance consultancy at 272 Bath Street. Scottish Energy Services provides commercial and domestic EPCs, display energy certificates, SAP and SBEM calculations, Section 63 assessments, TM59 overheating assessments, dynamic simulation modelling and legionella risk assessments, across Scotland and the north of England.

Fire Risk Scotland was set up as a dedicated specialist for fire risk assessment, so that landlords, businesses and factors looking for fire safety find a company focused entirely on it. If the same property needs an EPC, a legionella risk assessment or energy calculations, both companies can work together to arrange it with one visit and one point of contact.
Visit Scottish Energy Services
